kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Borrowed; considered even by the medievals as from Persian رَخْت (raxt). Though the term could be explained from an Aramaic descendant of Proto-Semitic *raḥat- (“flat inner of the hand”) transferred to refer to various flat tools, if the Arabic had been borrowed directly it would probably have become **رَحْت (**raḥt).
g: apparatus, goods and chattels of a household
apparel, vestment, plumage (including of a bird)
